backports.source: Omreq cancellation/total deadline/FIFO fixtures with exhausted peer MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS
backports.reason: Observe queued and pending-open request callback cancellation independently of peer stream capacity. Move existing queued messages into a cooperative FIFO and drop cancelled bodies without closing unrelated streams. Combined channel/FIFO ownership remains bounded by Omreq operation admission; no request/body copies or additional tasks are created.
regressions: T08/T09/T17 blocked Blob abort and total deadline
T08/T09/T16 cancelled tails behind a live FIFO head, surviving FIFO order and neighbour connection reuse
backports.removeWhen: Qualified upstream releases all cancelled queued and pending-open bodies while peer stream capacity remains exhausted, preserving live neighbours and FIFO order.

backports.source: Omreq ownership regression: paused server during multipart upload and cancelled response receiver
backports.reason: Return a cancelled dispatcher error when its response receiver is gone, rather than waiting for shutdown to flush a blocked request body. This drops the owned upload body and physical socket promptly without draining an aborted HTTP1 request.
regressions: T08 active multipart abort/close against a server paused after the first request bytes
Core upload-body task guard and physical TCP counters at cleanup
backports.removeWhen: Qualified upstream cancellation drops the dispatcher and blocked raw socket without waiting for peer read progress, with the same cancellation/reuse/wire regressions passing.

backports.source: Omreq implementation over the pinned wreq TCP creation and pool-race paths
backports.reason: Reserve capacity before every raw TCP socket including Happy Eyeballs attempts, release after raw socket drop and support owner-initiated close. A connect that loses the pool race to an idle connection completes in the background into the pool, marked by socket::is_raced_connect so the owner abandons it while it still waits for capacity instead of leaving an orphaned waiter. Also expose the separate inner reused-connection cancelled-request replay switch so Omreq can disable it alongside the outer retry policy. Upstream defaults remain unchanged without explicit options.
backports.removeWhen: Qualified upstream exposes equivalent physical socket lifetime hooks and bounded pool-race cancellation, verified by the same socket/resource and wire tests.

backports.reason: Expose the two native options required by the captured Chrome 157 reference without replacing the transport or using wreq-util enums.
backports.removeWhen: A qualified published wreq exposes these options with equivalent semantics and passes the same local wire tests.

backports.source: Omreq implementation; RFC 7541 section 5.2 and controlled Chrome 157 fresh/reused wire comparison
backports.reason: Expose a per-connection smaller-only Huffman policy. Preserve upstream always-Huffman behavior by default. Chrome uses plain strings when Huffman does not shrink them.
regressions: Live Chrome/Node/Bun exact HTTP2 preface through two HEADERS frames comparison
backports.removeWhen: Qualified upstream exposes an equivalent per-connection policy and passes the same tests.

backports.source: Omreq audit S-01: dual-stack host with a hung IPv6 path under maxConnectionsPerOrigin
backports.reason: Reserve socket capacity once per logical connect. Happy Eyeballs candidates of the same connect share the reservation, so a fallback never queues behind its own hung first attempt for the only slot. Overcommit is bounded by the parallel-attempt limit; the winning socket keeps the reservation.
backports.removeWhen: Qualified upstream exposes logical-connect capacity hooks that race candidates under one reservation.

backports.source: Omreq audit S-02: CONTINUATION buffering without an advertised SETTINGS_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE
backports.reason: Bound the received header block (CONTINUATION buffer and decoded list) to 256 KiB whether or not SETTINGS advertise MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE, and cap larger advertised values locally. SETTINGS frames sent are unchanged, so profile fingerprints are preserved.
backports.removeWhen: Qualified upstream exposes a local-only receive header list limit.

backports.reason: The btls revision with the QUIC TLS interface drops set_aes_hw_override and set_preserve_tls13_cipher_list and adds a parameter to add_application_settings. TLS 1.3 suites from the profile cipher list are set with set_tls13_ciphers in the same order; the TCP ClientHello stays byte-identical to the captured Chrome reference.
regressions: pnpm profile:qualify TLS, HTTP/2, HTTP/1 and resumption comparisons
backports.removeWhen: A qualified published wreq builds against a btls release with the QUIC interface.

backports.reason: Optional chaos protection of client Initial packets: the first packet carries the head and tail of a multi-packet ClientHello, CRYPTO data is split into random fragments with PING frames and spread PADDING, and frames are shuffled. With a shuffled transport parameter list, GREASE versions take random positions in version_information while real versions keep their order. Like QUICHE's PacingSender, the first ten packets are not paced, so a ClientHello spanning several datagrams leaves in one flight, and packets may be numbered from one sequence starting at 1 across all packet number spaces. The QUIC bit is greased only when the endpoint advertises grease_quic_bit itself.
regressions: quic-proto chaos layout and pacing unit tests (pnpm test:transport)
QUIC Initial comparison with Chrome in pnpm profile:qualify and tests/http3.test.mjs
backports.removeWhen: Upstream quic exposes equivalent Initial packet layout and version_information ordering options.

backports.reason: Omreq writes its own HTTP/3 request layer to match Chromium's control stream and QPACK encoding, and reuses the vendored QPACK decoder for dynamic-table responses. The decoder constructor, the resumable field-section decode and the buffered encoder-stream input become public; behaviour is unchanged.
regressions: HTTP/3 fixture tests with dynamic QPACK responses
backports.removeWhen: Upstream http3 exposes its QPACK decoder.

tls.reason: Pinned upstream implementation of signature-algorithm GREASE, ML-DSA, Trust Anchor IDs and the QUIC TLS interface used by the HTTP/3 transport, including its pinned BoringSSL source.
